title: When the Current Falls
premise: Elodie Montrose, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a disaster she didn't cause, has spent twenty years measuring life in miles rather than years. When her old rival Tomas Vey hires her crew for a forbidden crossing of the Karveth Range — the same route where her father died and where a stolen inheritance ledger is hidden — she breaks the oath that kept her alive. Racing the snows ahead of an early monsoon, pursued by the men who framed her father, Elodie discovers the ledger names the living heirs to a fortune built on erased villages. She reaches the pass as the storm breaks, delivers the truth to the last heir, and finally lets herself be measured in years instead of miles.
about_author: Casper Amberdale is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade planning high-altitude routes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who trust maps more than memories.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In a border-town outfitter's shop, Elodie takes a routine supply contract and deflects a journalist asking about the disaster twenty years ago. Her crew teases her about never celebrating birthdays. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — a life deliberately kept shallow so it can't break again.

chapters.title: The Rival's Letter
chapters.summary: Tomas Vey arrives unannounced with a permit stamped by a government that banned her. He offers triple pay for a crossing of the Karveth Range — the route sworn off since her father's death. Elodie refuses; her second-in-command, Priya, quietly accepts on the crew's behalf. Emotional beat: old fury reignited, and the first crack in her control.

chapters.title: What the Crew Decides
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew votes: half are deep in debt, one needs surgery money, all know the Karveth job would restore their reputation. Priya argues they deserve the chance Elodie was denied. Elodie relents but sets hard terms. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival, and Elodie realizing she can't protect everyone by saying no.

chapters.title: The Ledger He Carries
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. On the trailhead approach, Tomas reveals part of his motive: his dying uncle confessed to carrying a ledger off the mountain twenty years ago — records of land seizures disguised as the disaster's aftermath. Tomas wants it found before the men who made it do. Emotional beat: guilt worn as ambition; he needs Elodie's forgiveness more than her skills.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The crossing begins. Weather stations report an early monsoon forming over the coast — weeks ahead of schedule. Elodie recalculates every leg of the route and cuts their margin in half. A young porter, Dev, struggles; she teaches him to read the mountain instead of fearing it. Emotional beat: the return of purpose, and dread at what the sky is promising.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The team camps above a valley where maps show nothing, but stone foundations and a shrine say otherwise — one of the erased villages from the ledger's pages. An old shepherd tells them soldiers burned it after the disaster. Emotional beat: grief for the dead rendered invisible, and the dawning sense that this climb is about justice, not cargo.

chapters.title: Men on the Back Trail
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev spots armed men following their route — hired by the consortium named in the ledger. The crew debates turning back; Elodie refuses, realizing retreat through the followers is more dangerous than the climb. They cache supplies and split into two rope teams. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Dev grows from liability to lookout.

chapters.title: Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A technical set-piece: the team crosses a collapsing icefall at night to lose the pursuers. A ladder bridge fails under Tomas; Elodie anchors him on instinct, saving the man she swore to hate. Emotional beat: muscle memory of trust overriding twenty years of grudge.

chapters.title: Camp of Confessions
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Storm-bound in tents, Tomas admits his uncle helped falsify the disaster report that blacklisted Elodie's father — the ledger could clear his name posthumously. Elodie walks out into the wind rather than answer. Emotional beat: the wound reopened properly for the first time; anger becoming something closer to mourning.

chapters.title: The Father's Route Notes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In a cached depot her father left decades ago, Elodie finds his handwritten route notes — including a marked cairn 'where the truth sleeps.' Priya watches Elodie read them and understands the oath was never cowardice; it was a promise. Emotional beat: tenderness between friends, and Elodie choosing to finish her father's work.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The monsoon's leading edge hits early as heavy wet snow. Visibility drops to arm's length; the pursuers' camp is buried — two survivors stumble into the team's camp begging shelter. Elodie feeds them. Emotional beat: mercy as strength; even enemies are just cold men on a mountain.

chapters.title: The Bargain at High Camp
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. One survivor, a former surveyor, offers the location of the cairn in exchange for being walked down alive. He confirms the consortium's lawyer is already climbing from the other side. Elodie agrees — justice means witnesses, not corpses. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism warmed by principle.

chapters.title: The Cairn Where Truth Sleeps
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. At the marked cairn they find a sealed tin box: the full ledger, her father's final letter, and photographs of the seized villages. Her father knew he wouldn't come down and left the truth for whoever had the courage to climb for it. Emotional beat: communion with the dead; Elodie weeps openly for the first time in the book.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The consortium's party reaches them at the col — lawyers, guides, and muscle demanding the ledger as 'stolen property.' Negotiation turns to standoff on knife-edge ground where no one can fight safely. Emotional beat: tension held in stillness; violence would kill everyone, and both sides know it.

chapters.title: The Long Traverse
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie proposes a gamble: a traverse no guide has survived, which will let them bypass the blockade and descend toward the valley town where the last living heir lives. The pursuers must follow or die waiting. Emotional beat: audacity born of mastery — the blacklist taught her routes no legitimate guide would dare.

chapters.title: Dev's Ledge
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The traverse's crux: Dev freezes on an exposed ledge as rockfall begins. Elodie talks him across step by step, voice steady while her hands shake. They make the far side as the ledge collapses behind them. Emotional beat: mentorship fulfilled; Dev stops being a student and becomes a climber.

chapters.title: Storm Wall
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The full monsoon makes landfall. The team shelters in a crevasse city for thirty hours, rationing fuel, listening to the mountain roar. Tomas and Elodie finally speak plainly — not forgiveness yet, but a truce with honest weight. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in confinement; the grudge dissolving into shared purpose.

chapters.title: Descent Into Green
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. They break below the snowline into monsoon rain and terraced fields. The pursuers have fallen behind, but word travels faster than climbers — the consortium has sent agents to the valley town. The race becomes legal and human now, not vertical. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by urgency; the mountain was the easy part.

chapters.title: The Last Heir
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the valley town they find Meera, an elderly schoolteacher descended from the erased village's headman — the rightful heir to restitution claims the ledger documents. Agents arrive to buy her silence. Elodie hands her the ledger publicly, before witnesses at the market. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; justice delivered outside any courtroom, hand to hand.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. With the ledger public, the former surveyor testifies, and the crew's account spreads. The consortium's local partners collapse; the blacklist against Elodie's father is formally reviewed. Tomas offers to take sole blame for hiring her illegally. Emotional beat: accountability accepted without flinching; honor reconstructed piece by piece.

chapters.title: When the Current Falls
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax and catharsis at the waterfall where her father's route notes end: the 'current' of the title, falling past the rebuilt village shrine. Elodie scatters his ashes there, reads his letter aloud, and lets the crew see her cry. The pursuers' last threat dissolves when Meera files the restitution claim with international observers present. Emotional beat: release — twenty years of frozen grief finally moving like water.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Priya's POV. One year later: the crew runs a licensed guide service training local youth, including Dev as junior instructor. Elodie celebrates her birthday for the first time in twenty years, on the anniversary of the descent. Tomas sends a letter she reads twice and keeps. Emotional beat: homecoming — a life measured in years, shared with people, at last.
